q: In physics, work is defined as the product of force and _____ moved in the direction of the force.
e: Work is defined as the product of force and distance moved in the direction of the force.

q: The mathematical expression for work done is _____.
e: The formula for work done is the product of force (F) and distance (s).
Work has magnitude but no direction, making it a scalar quantity.

q: The SI unit of work is the _____.
e: The SI unit for both work and energy is the joule (J).

q: 1 joule of work is done when a force of 1 newton moves an object through a distance of _____ in the direction of the force.
When the unit of force is in pound (lb) and the distance is in foot (ft), the unit of work is _____.
e: The foot-pound (ft-lb) is the imperial unit of work.

q: When the unit of force is in dyne and the distance is in centimetre, the unit of work is _____.
e: The erg is the CGS unit of work.

q: The relationship between joule and erg is _____.
When the force is constant, and the direction of the force makes an angle $\theta$ with that of motion, work is defined as _____.
e: Only the component of force in the direction of motion ($F \cos \theta$) does work.

q: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When force and motion are in the same direction, the angle between them is $0^{\circ}$.

q: When the directions of the force and the motion are the same, the work done is _____.
e: Since $\cos 0^{\circ} = 1$, the work done is simply $W = Fs$.

q: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When force and motion are in opposite directions, the angle between them is $180^{\circ}$.

q: When the force and the motion are in opposite directions, the work done is _____.
e: Since $\cos 180^{\circ} = -1$, the work done is negative, $W = -Fs$.

q: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the angle $\theta$ is _____.
e: When force and motion are perpendicular, the angle between them is $90^{\circ}$.

q: When the force and the motion are perpendicular to each other, the work done is _____.
e: Since $\cos 90^{\circ} = 0$, no work is done when force is perpendicular to motion.
